entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6197"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 65</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.65.1-Ps.65.13">Psa 65:1-13</reference>. This is a song of praise for God's spiritual blessings to His people and His kind providence over all the earth.</title> <div sID="gen9477" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6197"/><hi type="bold">1. Praise waiteth for thee--</hi>literally, "To Thee silence praise," or (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.62.1">Psa 62:1</reference>), To Thee silence is praise--that is, Praise is waiting as a servant; it is due to Thee. So the last clause expresses the duty of paying vows. These two parts of acceptable worship, mentioned in <reference osisRef="Ps.50.14">Psa 50:14</reference>, are rendered in Zion, where God chiefly displays His mercy and receives homage. <div eID="gen9477" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6202"/><div sID="gen9485" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6202"/>6-13. God's great power and goodness are the grounds of this confidence. These are illustrated in His control of the mightiest agencies of nature and nations affecting men with awe and dread (<reference osisRef="Ps.26.7">Psa 26:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.98.1">98:1</reference>, &c.), and in His fertilizing showers, causing the earth to produce abundantly for man and beast. <div eID="gen9485" type="x-p"/>
